## What's Changed
* docs: clarify getting started and showcase Predictions Setup by @fcoouto in https://github.com/fcoouto/opencode-predictions/pull/26
* feat: make prediction settings writable through server preferences by @fcoouto in https://github.com/fcoouto/opencode-predictions/pull/28
* feat!: use only prediction preferences by @fcoouto in https://github.com/fcoouto/opencode-predictions/pull/29
* fix: default predictions to a 30s timeout by @fcoouto in https://github.com/fcoouto/opencode-predictions/pull/30
* [READY] feat(desktop): add manual prediction hint by @fcoouto in https://github.com/fcoouto/opencode-predictions/pull/27
* [READY] fix(desktop): polish manual prediction hint by @fcoouto in https://github.com/fcoouto/opencode-predictions/pull/31
* [READY] feat(setup): move Reset to defaults above Save and drop User preferences section by @fcoouto in https://github.com/fcoouto/opencode-predictions/pull/32
* [READY] fix(client): stay quiet while a new location's status RPC boots by @fcoouto in https://github.com/fcoouto/opencode-predictions/pull/33
* [READY] chore: prepare v0.4.0 release by @fcoouto in https://github.com/fcoouto/opencode-predictions/pull/34


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/fcoouto/opencode-predictions/compare/v0.3.0...v0.4.0

## Highlights

- **Try another model:** request untried eligible models in the current group before later groups with **Alt+Shift+P** (**Option+Shift+P** on macOS).
- **Automatic error fallback:** provider failures, invalid responses and model timeouts advance through remaining eligible models, including during explicit alternatives. Genuine null responses follow the configured abstention policy.
- **Clearer progress and recovery:** compact progress names the actual attempted model; next-model guidance appears only after real abstention, not provider failure or metadata refresh.
- **Completed-reply context:** predictions work after synthetic continuations and compaction without requiring a new user message. Synthetic instructions, reasoning, tool output and compaction summaries remain excluded.
- **Readable Desktop previews:** the composer grows to fit up to six visible prediction lines, ellipsizes longer previews and restores normal height when dismissed. Tab still accepts the full prediction without submitting it.

Cancellation, stale-context checks, cooldowns, tried-model tracking and retained-original recovery remain in place. Additional safeguards prevent stale progress and removed catalog models from causing incorrect or repeated requests.

## Install

Use `github:fcoouto/opencode-predictions#v0.2.0` in the `plugins` array of your existing OpenCode configuration. See the [README](https://github.com/fcoouto/opencode-predictions/blob/v0.2.0/README.md) for settings, controls and privacy details.

The attached `opencode-predictions-0.2.0.tgz` is the prebuilt package. `SHA256SUMS` records its SHA-256 checksum. Installation requires no build scripts.

## Verification

- 230 unit/rendered tests, typecheck, production bundle, package validation and whitespace checks passed.
- The attached archive passed 28 installed-package checks: real isolated Desktop 13/13, CLI PTY 10/10, server RPC 4/4 and Git installation 1/1.
- Native Desktop and CLI gates ran sequentially. They use synthetic local providers and do not alter the user's installed plugin.
- Every packed file byte-matches the release source tree, and the archive's SHA-256 checksum was verified.
- The release-preparation pull request passed GitHub Actions before merge.

## Compatibility and limits

Requires OpenCode V2 and Node.js 26.4.0 or newer. Desktop integration uses an experimental API.

Prediction calls may consume provider quota or paid tokens. Error fallback can call several models in one action; OpenCode/provider transport retries remain outside plugin control. Cancellation does not guarantee avoiding provider charges.

The selected provider receives filtered visible conversation text, which can contain sensitive information. No paid-provider quality experiments were performed for this release. Existing status truncation and mixed-error wording limitations are unchanged.

### npm publication status

GitHub release assets and the pinned GitHub installation are available. The tag workflow passed its tests, build, package and version checks, but npm publication failed with `E404` for `opencode-predictions@0.2.0` (“could not be found or you do not have permission to access it”). This release is not published to npm; no registry credentials or publishing settings were changed.

## First release

OpenCode Predictions suggests a useful next user prompt as editable ghost text in OpenCode Desktop and the interactive CLI.

### Highlights

- Automatic suggestions after completed responses, plus manual requests with Alt+Shift+P or the command palette.
- Tab inserts a suggestion for editing without submitting it. Suggestions survive edits and chat navigation without another model call.
- A concise next-step directive that respects explicit constraints and unfinished delivery work.
- Ordered model groups, fallback selection, cooldowns, and actionable error/status views.
- Prebuilt server, CLI, and experimental Desktop entries; installation requires no build scripts.

### Install

Add `github:fcoouto/opencode-predictions#v0.1.0` to the `plugins` array in your existing OpenCode configuration. See the [README](https://github.com/fcoouto/opencode-predictions/blob/v0.1.0/README.md) for model configuration, controls, and privacy/cost details.

The attached `opencode-predictions-0.1.0.tgz` is the package used for the installed-artifact checks. `SHA256SUMS` records its checksum.

### Verification

- 160 tests, type checking, bundling, repeat-build consistency, and package validation passed locally.
- Nine installed-artifact checks passed across the real Desktop, CLI, server, and Git installation paths.
- Tested with OpenCode CLI 2.2.6 and Desktop 2.2.7 on macOS. Requires OpenCode V2 and Node.js 26.4.0 or newer. Desktop integration uses an experimental API.
- The release commit passed the GitHub Actions Check workflow before publication.

### Security and limitations

Vite is pinned to 7.3.8, clearing the previously reported high-severity Vite advisories. No high or critical findings remained in the checked repository or installed-package audits. Vite was absent from the clean installed runtime package tree.

Moderate upstream dependency findings remain: npm audit reported 24 moderate entries for the repository and 25 for the installed package tree, including propagated dependency findings. These counts are not independent vulnerabilities. They have not been fully remediated or proven unreachable.

Predictions can consume provider quota or paid tokens. The selected provider receives recent user and assistant text. OpenCode V1, Mini, browser-only clients, and noninteractive predictions are not supported.
